notes: Estimated vs. actual in Analytics now compares whole tasks, not individual sittings. It used to plot every study session as its own dot, so a three-hour task done in three sittings showed up as three dots that each looked like you had finished early, and dragged your estimate accuracy down to around 60% for a task you had estimated exactly right. Now each finished task is one dot: its estimate against every minute you logged on it. Tasks don't appear until they're done, and ones you ticked off without timing are left out, since there's nothing to compare.

XP had the same problem and is fixed the same way. Working on a task over several sittings could earn nothing for a later sitting, because it was measured against only what was left of the estimate. Now the overrun rule looks at the task's total, and the good-estimate bonus is awarded once, when the task is finished. Your XP is recalculated from your history, so your total may move a little.
The workload forecast now shows the time still to do on each task rather than its full estimate, so it agrees with the scheduler about how busy a day is once you've started something.
Loading the sample data or restoring a backup no longer sends you back through first-run setup the next time you open the app.
On phones, pages use the full width of the screen again. About a quarter of it had been kept empty on the right to stay clear of the coach button.
